@lcv-leo, thank you for the report. You traced the bug to the exact line in `resolveWorktreeCandidates`, and you'd already written and verified a patch, so this PR builds on your fix. Earlier today [I asked](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/2979#issuecomment-6618856546) whether you planned to open a PR, and asked @peyton-alt to assign the issue to me if you weren't. I'm opening this now because I have the fix reproduced, with tests that fail on `main` and pass here. If you'd rather open your own PR, just say so and I'll close this one.

## What was wrong

If you commit from a worktree that has no Entire session, the CLI falls back to sessions from other worktrees of the same repo. `resolveWorktreeCandidates` only checks the 15-minute `recentSessionWindow` when those sessions come from more than one worktree. If they all come from one worktree, it links them without checking, no matter how long they've been idle. In the report, a Codex session that had been idle for over a day got linked to every commit made from another worktree. Each time, `post-commit` condensed its 5 GB transcript.

## The fix

`findSessionsForCommitLinking` now runs the fallback's matches through `withoutIdleSessions`. It drops a session whose last interaction is older than `recentSessionWindow`. These sessions are kept:

- a session with no recorded interaction, as before, because we don't know how long it's been idle;
- a session that's mid-turn (active phase, turn started within `activeSessionInteractionThreshold`), because `LastInteractionTime` only changes at turn boundaries;
- a session with a background subagent still running (`hasFreshLiveTaskRecord`), the same case `idleWithLiveTaskRecord` already trusts;
- a session that recorded edits in the committing worktree, which still joins through its worktree entry, limited to those edits.

Amend and post-rewrite use `findSessionsForWorktree` to keep existing links up to date, and they don't change. The multi-worktree path doesn't change either.

Here's how this differs from the patch in the issue. Review on my fork found that putting the check inside `resolveWorktreeCandidates` also hid idle sibling sessions from amend and post-rewrite. It also dropped sessions that were mid-turn or had a subagent running. So the check now runs only for commit linking, and it keeps those two cases. The drop is logged at Debug, without `idle_for`. I'm happy to switch to the Info line from your patch if you prefer it.

## Tests

New file `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/worktree_idle_fallback_test.go`:

- `TestCommitLinking_FallbackSkipsSiblingSessionsIdleBeyondTheWindow`: idle for a day, idle just past the window, recent, no recorded interaction, mid-turn past the window, left active for two days, idle with a subagent in flight, idle with a finished subagent, and stale next to recent and undated.
- `TestCommitLinking_IdleSiblingSessionThatEditedHereStillJoins`
- `TestPostRewrite_StillRemapsAnIdleSiblingSession`

On `main` with only the test file added, 5 subtests fail. The last two tests pass there; they guard behaviour that must not change:

```
--- FAIL: TestCommitLinking_FallbackSkipsSiblingSessionsIdleBeyondTheWindow
    --- FAIL: .../idle_for_a_day
    --- FAIL: .../idle_just_past_the_window
    --- PASS: .../recent
    --- PASS: .../no_recorded_interaction
    --- PASS: .../mid-turn_past_the_window
    --- FAIL: .../left_active_for_two_days
    --- PASS: .../idle_with_a_subagent_in_flight
    --- FAIL: .../idle_with_a_finished_subagent
    --- FAIL: .../stale_beside_recent_and_undated
--- PASS: TestCommitLinking_IdleSiblingSessionThatEditedHereStillJoins
--- PASS: TestPostRewrite_StillRemapsAnIdleSiblingSession
FAIL
```

On this branch, all 12 pass.

## What I ran

I ran these on this exact tree in a clean `env -i` with a throwaway HOME, Go 1.27.3 and git 2.56:

- `go vet`, then `go test -count=1` of `./cmd/entire/cli/strategy/` and `./cmd/entire/cli/`: pass.
- `go test -race` on `strategy`: pass. Windows `go vet` and a Windows test build of `strategy`: pass.
- `mise run lint`: 0 issues.
- Complexity gate, run the way CI runs it (`BASE_REF=711697ee5 mise run complexity:gate`): pass.
- A one-off check of the nested layout (`.worktrees/nested` under the main checkout): an idle session in the main checkout isn't linked, and a recent one is. That test isn't in this PR.

## Review on my fork

Before opening this, I had the review bots go over it on my fork. "Ran" means I reproduced the finding with a test before changing anything.

- Kilo, first commit: a sibling session mid-turn for over 15 minutes was dropped. Ran: confirmed, fixed, and covered by `mid-turn_past_the_window`.
- Kilo, first commit: the check also hid idle sibling sessions from amend and post-rewrite. Ran: confirmed with a post-rewrite test, fixed by moving the check to commit linking, and covered by `TestPostRewrite_StillRemapsAnIdleSiblingSession`.
- Kilo and Codex, second commit: an idle session with a background subagent still running was dropped. Ran: confirmed, fixed, and covered by `idle_with_a_subagent_in_flight`.
- Baz noted that a turn longer than 24h still drops out. Read-only: I didn't change it, because that's the same limit `activeSessionInteractionThreshold` sets everywhere else.
- On the final head: Codex, Kilo and Greptile reported no issues. Gitar and CodeRabbit didn't review because of plan limits on my fork.

The commit has no `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.

## Open questions, possible follow-ups

These came from the issue. I kept them out of this PR so it stays small:

1. **Sessions with no recorded interaction.** They're still linked, as on `main`. Should the fallback drop them too?
2. **Hint message.** A dropped idle session is only logged. The ambiguous multi-worktree case prints an `entire session adopt` hint. Do you want a one-line hint here too, given the concern in #1852 about losing links silently? It would show up on every terminal commit while an agent sits idle in another worktree.
3. **Nested `.worktrees/` case.** A worktree under the main checkout matches the parent checkout's sessions through `parentWorktreeMatches`, and this check applies there too. I checked that by hand but didn't add a test for it. Should that layout get the same treatment and its own test?

`SanitizePathForCursor` builds the name of Cursor's project directory (`~/.cursor/projects/<name>`) from the repo path, but not the way Cursor does. Cursor collapses runs of non-alphanumeric characters into one `-` and trims `-` from both ends; Entire only stripped the leading `/` and replaced each character separately. Any path with two separators in a row (a `.worktrees` checkout, `/-…` segments) or any Windows path (`C:\…` → `C--…`) got a directory Cursor never writes to.

Everything Entire computes from that directory is then wrong: resume restores a transcript where Cursor never reads it, attach and history import look in the wrong place, transcript discovery misses the session, and a transcript under Cursor's real directory isn't recognised as Cursor's. Cursor's hooks send `transcript_path: null` until the transcript file exists, so on a session's first turn the turn start computes the path, and the wrong one stays in session state until the next hook carries the real path.

On this machine, Entire's rule names 60 of the 78 Cursor project directories correctly (from their `.workspace-trusted` files); all 18 misses are worktrees or `--` paths. Windows paths are affected too (`C:\repo` → `C--repo`, Cursor uses `C-repo`).

## Change

- `SanitizePathForCursor` now matches Cursor's rule exactly, taken from cursor-agent's `workspace-paths.js` (2026.10.22; the IDE ships the same function): `t.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g,"-").replace(/-+/g,"-").replace(/^-+|-+$/g,"")`. ASCII-only, case kept. It matches all 78 directories on this machine.
- History import's repo-boundary walk (`pathsWithEncoding`, which refuses transcripts whose project directory another repo also maps to) assumed one output character per path character. With collapsing and trimming, a directory can encode to nothing or to the target itself and still lead to a match, so the walk now descends into those too. It stays fail-closed: if the walk hits its read limit, the transcript is treated as shared and not imported.
- Comments that said "the CLI sends a null transcript_path" now say it's null until the transcript exists, in both the IDE and the CLI.

No fallback to the old naming: Cursor never wrote under it, so nothing on disk depends on it. Resume now writes into the directory Cursor actually reads (still guarded by the existing-log check and `--force`).

## Tests

- Sanitizer table with collapsing, trimming, Windows, worktree and case rows; a parity table whose expected values come from running Cursor's own function (empty, `/`, `-`, `/a/`, non-ASCII letters, emoji, NUL, `C:\x`, `C:/x`).
- `GetSessionDir` for a `.worktrees` repo with a temp `HOME`.
- First turn: a repo under `<tmp>/a/.worktrees/repo`, the transcript where Cursor writes it, and a `stop` with `transcript_path: null` resolves to that file.
- Import walk: checked against a brute-force enumeration of a small tree, and a collision that only exists under Cursor's rule (`x/.wt/r` vs `x/wt/r`).
- Import walk: the volume root is a candidate too (`/` encodes like `/---` under the new rule).
- All new tests fail on main; the walk test also fails with the new rule and the old walk.
- **Live, cursor-agent 2026.10.22 (Auto → Claude Haiku), a repo under `…/proj/.worktrees/repo`, three turns and a commit:** on main the first turn start computed `…-proj--worktrees-repo` while Cursor wrote to `…-proj-worktrees-repo`; with this change Entire computes Cursor's directory. On this version the stop hook already carries the real `transcript_path` on the first turn, so turn 1 was recorded on both builds; with this change the session's token totals equal the sum of Cursor's stop-hook usage exactly. An earlier live session (Oct 19, older setup) lost its first checkpoint to this mismatch; that wasn't reproduced on the current CLI.
- **Live, resume and attach** (one cursor-agent session in a `…/proj/.worktrees/repo` test repo, Entire enabled afterwards): `entire session resume --force` wrote the transcript to `…-proj--worktrees-repo/agent-transcripts/` on main, a directory Cursor never reads, and to Cursor's `…-proj-worktrees-repo/agent-transcripts/` with this change. `entire session attach` succeeded on both, but on main only through the fallback search across `~/.cursor/projects` ("found transcript in alternative project directory"); with this change the computed path hits directly.
- The existing Cursor integration tests set `ENTIRE_TEST_CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR`, which bypasses the sanitizer; that's why CI never caught this.

## Not in this PR

- Resume restores the transcript as `agent-transcripts/<id>.jsonl`, while Cursor writes `agent-transcripts/<id>/<id>.jsonl`, so Cursor may still not pick up a resumed session (same on main).

- A session started before upgrading that never gets another turn keeps its old stored path.
- A workspace opened through a symlinked path (`/tmp` vs `/private/tmp`) still differs from the git root Entire uses; Cursor names the directory after the path as opened.

One of the per-agent token fixes; each is its own PR off main.

Builds on #3075, which made every Windows hook wrapper look programs up on PATH only. The Windows commands here are built from that PR's wrappers. What this adds on top is Codex's native `commandWindows`, preservation of fields Entire doesn't model, and trust coverage for the Windows command.

AppSolves validated this head on native Windows with Codex 0.169 alpha ([results](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/3163#issuecomment-6989812055)); see "Tested on real Windows" below.

## What this changes

- **Native `commandWindows` on every managed Codex hook.** `.codex/hooks.json` keeps the POSIX `command` as it is and adds `commandWindows`, which Codex runs instead of `command` on Windows. The file is now the same on every host, so a checkout shared between macOS, Linux and Windows no longer gets rewritten by whichever machine ran `entire enable` last.
- **Windows commands that parse in both Codex Windows shells.** Silent hooks use main's `WrapWindowsProductionSilentHookCommand`: `cmd.exe /d /s /c "set NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1& pushd %SystemRoot%& where.exe entire >nul 2>nul & if errorlevel 1 (popd& ...) else (popd& ...)"`. The quoted body has no `"`, `$` or backtick, and its only variable is `%SystemRoot%`, which the outer cmd.exe expands and PowerShell leaves for the inner one. So PowerShell (Codex's default Windows hook shell) and `%COMSPEC% /C` (its fallback) both pass it to cmd.exe unchanged. The direct cmd form main writes into `command` when the sh probe fails, `... & if errorlevel 1 (popd& echo {^"...) else (...)`, does not parse under PowerShell.
- **SessionStart warning on Windows is plain text.** The new `WrapWindowsProductionNestedPlainTextWarningHookCommand` is the same nested PATH-only form with a warning. No JSON warning survives both shells inside that wrapper, and Codex already shows plain SessionStart stdout as context, so a missing `entire` binary is still reported. Like the POSIX wrapper, it also probes `entire --version` and prints the failed-CLI warning for a shim with no version selected. ## What changes on Windows

`proclive` returned "unsupported" on Windows (#1488 left it out of scope). So until now:

- **Liveness** of a mid-turn session was always unknown. `entire status`, `entire doctor`, attach and the exited-owner sweep fell back to `IsStuckActive`, which counts a turn over an hour as stuck even while its agent still runs.
- **Commit provenance** never marked a session foreign. With no TTY, `prepare-commit-msg`'s fast path stamped any mid-turn session, so a script's commit during another session's turn went to that session.

With this PR, a Windows session records its agent's process as owner at turn start, `Check` reports it alive or dead, and a commit hook's ancestry walk can show that a live owner is not its ancestor, as on Linux and macOS. That should make @mattjes's Windows baseline (https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/3053#issuecomment-6706927443) come out as it does on Linux, where the first row gives no trailer instead of A.

## How

A `proc_windows.go` behind the existing seam:

- `procStat` opens the process with `PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION`. It reads the parent PID (`NtQueryInformationProcess`), the creation time (`GetProcessTimes`) and the image name (`QueryFullProcessImageName`). The creation time is the start fingerprint. It's absolute, like darwin's, so `bootID` returns no guard.
- An exited process that some handle still holds counts as gone: its handle is signaled, or its exit code is no longer `STILL_ACTIVE`. The handle check also catches a process that exited with 259 as its code. It needs `SYNCHRONIZE`. Where a process's DACL denies that, a process whose exit code still reads `STILL_ACTIVE` is reported as unknown, not alive.
- **Where a walk ends.** Windows keeps a process's parent PID after the parent exits, and the PID can then be reused, so no walk reaches an init. `procStat` therefore checks the parent too. If the parent has exited, or its PID now names a process created after the child, `procStat` reports PID 1, where `walkAncestry` already ends a complete chain. Windows never assigns PID 1. The chain up to the first process without a living parent holds every living ancestor, which is what `Ancestry.Complete` needs to mean on Windows. It is also what Linux and macOS give when a parent exits mid-chain: the child is reparented to init, and the walk reaches PID 1 without the processes above it. Creation order comes from the process sequence number, which the kernel counts per boot, so a clock change can't reorder it. Where the system doesn't report one (older Windows versions, Wine), the creation time stands in.
- A parent it can't open (another user's process, so access denied) is reported unverified. The walk then stops there incomplete, and `Excludes` proves nothing, as after any failed lookup.
- **Windows and WSL.** They can share a hostname and a checkout, so each can read the owners the other recorded, but their PIDs name different process tables. Every owner now records the OS of the binary that recorded it (`Identity.OS`). `Check`, `Depth` and `Excludes` treat an owner recorded for another OS as one they can't judge, so WSL's sweep can't end a live Windows session, and a Windows commit hook can't mark a WSL session foreign. Owners recorded before this carry no OS and are judged as before. Every turn start records a new owner, so only a turn that was already running at upgrade lacks one.
- `isTransient` ignores a `.exe` suffix and adds `cmd`, `powershell`, `pwsh` and `conhost`, so the owner is the agent, not the shell that ran the hook.

`doctor_classify_live_test.go` and `owner_wiring_test.go` now build on Windows too: they need nothing Unix-only. The two doctor tests now carry `Windows` in their names, so the `test-windows` job runs them. `TestInitializeSession_CapturesOwner` keeps its name for now, because no strategy test that builds a git repo runs on that job yet; it's in the test list below. The docs that said Windows can't introspect are updated.

## The risk

A wrong owner. If the first non-shell ancestor of a turn-start hook is a short-lived intermediary rather than the agent, the owner reads as dead while the agent still runs. `entire doctor` and the sweep would then end that session, and `entire status` would show it as exited. The same rule already holds on Linux and macOS. What's new is each agent's Windows hook chain, which I can't see from Linux. It needs a run with real agents on Windows before it merges.

- `Check` reads a live child as alive and the same child as dead once it exits. That includes while Go still holds its handle, which keeps an exited process and its PID in the table.

Fixes #1642 — on worktrees with large gitignored trees, the Claude Code `user-prompt-submit` hook takes 40–55s per prompt and every turn-end checkpoint pays the same cost again. Root cause: three hot paths still used go-git's `worktree.Status()`, which stats and hashes every file on disk including gitignored directories. Several sibling call sites had already been converted to the native git CLI for exactly this reason (see the existing comments in `checkpoint/ephemeral.go` and `getStagedFiles` in `strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`); this PR finishes the job.

## Changes

- **`strategy/common.go`**: new exported `GitCLIStatus(ctx)` helper — runs `git status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall --no-renames` at the worktree root and parses the output into a go-git-compatible `git.Status` map. Porcelain v1 status letters are byte-identical to go-git's `StatusCode` constants, so this is a drop-in replacement for `worktree.Status()`.
- **`state.go`**: `getUntrackedFilesForState` (→ `capture_pre_prompt_state`) and `DetectFileChanges` (→ turn-end checkpointing) now use `GitCLIStatus`.
- **`strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`**: `calculatePromptAttributionAtStart` (→ `init_session`) now uses `GitCLIStatus`.
- **`state_test.go`**: the hand-rolled test repos gain a `.git/refs/` directory — the native git CLI requires it to recognize a repository (go-git did not).

## Measurements

61GB / ~686k-file worktree (~34GB in gitignored SwiftPM `.build/` dirs), measured with `entire doctor trace` + `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `user-prompt-submit` total | 45,954ms | **193ms** |
| `capture_pre_prompt_state` | 24,397ms | 102ms |
| `init_session` | 21,540ms | 79ms |

Turn-end shadow-branch commits went from 20–50s to sub-second on the same repo.

- `mise run lint` — clean
- `mise run test` — 989 passed; the single failure (`TestRunUninstall_Force_NothingInstalled`) is pre-existing and environment-dependent — it fails identically on pristine `main` on any machine where the Entire CLI is installed, because the uninstall path finds a real installation.

## Notes

- No `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer on the commit: the investigation and patch were developed from an agent session anchored in the affected repo (where the bug lives), not this clone, so there was no checkpoint in this worktree to attribute. Happy to adjust if you'd like it structured differently.
- Issue #1642 was filed first per CONTRIBUTING.md; this PR is ready for whenever maintainers have looked at it.

External agents that are forks of built-in agents each ship their own `compact-transcript`, re-implementing a converter the CLI already has. Those copies drift: Sarvam Code's (a Codex fork) writes no per-call model or usage, and Oh My Pi's (Pi) writes no model. Detection can't stand in for them either: Oh My Pi writes a title line before the Pi header, so it's not recognised as Pi, and Kilo Code stores one OpenCode message per line rather than an export, so it converts to nothing.

## What

- **Protocol:** an optional `"transcript_format"` field in `info`. When an agent declares it, the CLI's built-in converter builds its `transcript.jsonl`, labelled with the agent's name, and takes precedence over the agent's own `compact-transcript`. That compactor runs only if the built-in conversion fails or comes out empty, so an agent can keep it for older CLIs, which ignore the field. A value this CLI doesn't know is ignored, so the CLI falls back to detecting the format. `opencode` (export) and `gemini` are ignored the same way for now: their checkpoint start is a message index, and condensation counts an external agent's transcript by line.
- **`transcript` library:**
  - `Options.Format` selects the converter instead of detecting it. The names match the built-in agents, plus `opencode-messages` (one `{"info","parts"}` message per line, never detected).
  - A declared `claude-code` gets per-call usage for any agent name.
  - A declared `pi` converts a session whose header isn't the first line.
- **Codex exit codes:** the `response_item` path now reads the `{"output","metadata":{"exit_code"}}` envelope that older Codex shell tools (and forks) write. A failed command becomes `status: error` with its `exitCode`, instead of `success` with the raw envelope as output. MCP tools (names with `__`) and objects with keys beyond `output` and `metadata` are left alone.
- **Wiring:** `InfoResponse.TranscriptFormat`, reached through `agent.AsTranscriptFormatProvider`. The checkpoint fallback passes the declared format.
- **Docs:** the protocol spec (`info` field, plus guidance under `compact_transcript`) and `transcript/README.md`.

## Testing

- **Unit:**
  - A declared format gives byte-identical output to detection for every fixture, at `StartLine` 0 and 3.
  - `claude-code` for another agent name.
  - Unknown format.
  - `opencode-messages` matches the export it came from.
  - A Pi session with a leading title line: detection fails, the declared format succeeds.
  - Four exit-envelope cases.
  - `info` with a known, unknown, or missing format.
  - Checkpoint: a declared format changes the stored `transcript.jsonl` (the model is present), and without it the model is missing.
  - Checkpoint precedence: a declared format beats the agent's own compactor, an empty declared conversion falls back to it, and with no declaration the compactor still runs first.
- **Against real agents' own fixtures:**
  - **Oh My Pi, declared `pi`:** matches its own converter and adds the model. It keeps native tool names (`Write`, `mcp:read`) where omp lowercases them and strips the `mcp:` prefix.
  - **Kilo, declared `opencode-messages`:** matches its own output.
- **Local end-to-end:**
  - A real `entire-agent-sarvam` binary, patched to declare `codex` with no compactor, ran through `entire enable`, simulated session-start, prompt and stop hooks, then a commit. The checkpoint's `transcript.jsonl` carries the model, per-call tokens and a failed command marked as an error.
  - The same agent against a released CLI still checkpoints, because the unknown field is ignored.
- **Suites:**
  - `mise run lint`: 0 issues.
  - `complexity:gate`: passes.
  - `go test -tags=integration -race ./...`: passes.
  - Integration suite: passes.
  - Canary: Vogon and roger-roger pass.
  - Under full-suite load, a few timing-sensitive tests in unrelated packages timed out (`claudecode`/`opencode` probes, fetch timeout). They pass when re-run individually.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `countTranscriptItems` should count messages for an external agent whose transcript is an OpenCode export or Gemini session (already wrong on main for detected ones). Then `opencode` and `gemini` can be declared.

- Summaries (`summarize.BuildCondensedTranscriptFromBytes`) still treat external agents as Claude-style JSONL.
- Agents in `entireio/external-agents` can opt in once a release with this ships. Oh My Pi is the clearest win, since it gains the model.

## Why

The `entire ci buildkite` subgroup shipped as a "coming soon" placeholder in
the scaffold PR. This turns it into the real operator surface for managing a
repo's Buildkite CI-webhook subscriptions through the core-mediated
management API (the ci-webhooks routes shipped in entire-core under COR-836).

The whole `ci` group stays gated behind the `internal` build tag, so none of
this appears in released `entire` binaries.

## What

Four verbs under `entire ci buildkite`, each resolving `<repo>` to a ULID via
the inherited `ResolveNativeRepo` (native `<project>/<repo>` path or a raw repo
ULID; GitHub mirrors rejected):

- `enroll <repo> [pipeline] --bk-org <slug> --bk-cluster-id <id> [--ref-filter <glob>] [--events create,update] [--display-name <s>]`
  → `POST /api/v1/repos/{repoId}/ci-webhooks` with `provider: buildkite`. The
  optional `[pipeline]` positional is omitted to let the server default it to
  the repo name. No token field — the Buildkite credential is operator-seeded,
  org-level. `--bk-org` is required; `--bk-cluster-id` is enforced by the
  server (a later PR resolves it via cluster discovery, so it is not marked
  required client-side yet). Prints `Enrolled` on a fresh 201 and `Re-enrolled`
  on an idempotent 200.
- `list <repo>` → `GET …/ci-webhooks`, rendered as an aligned table (id,
  provider, bk_org, pipeline, enabled, ref_filter, events) or raw `--json`.
- `update <repo> <subscriptionId> [--enabled=bool] [--ref-filter <glob>] [--events …] [--display-name <s>]`
  → `PATCH …/ci-webhooks/{id}`, sending **only** the flags the user set (cobra
  `Changed` checks; unset = unchanged). An explicit empty `--events` clears the
  list. A no-op update (no field flags) is rejected before any request.
- `remove <repo> <subscriptionId> [--teardown]` → `DELETE …/ci-webhooks/{id}?teardown=<bool>`
  (204). `--teardown` also revokes the enrollment identity; the Buildkite
  pipeline is always kept.

Because the `cli` package imports this one (`root.go` calls `ci.Register`), the
verbs can't reuse `cli`'s `runCore*` helpers — the package carries a small,
clearly-commented local `runCore` preamble and rendering helpers, mirroring how
the inherited `resolve.go` already replicates its control-plane helpers to avoid
the import cycle.

### coreapi client

No hand-written client and no full regen were needed: the base branch's spec
refresh already exposes `CreateRepoCIWebhook` / `ListRepoCIWebhooks` /
`PatchRepoCIWebhook` / `DeleteRepoCIWebhook` and their DTOs in
`internal/coreapi/`.

One targeted spec workaround was added and the client regenerated via the
documented `go generate ./internal/coreapi/...` path: the enroll `POST` is
idempotent (201 fresh / 200 re-enroll, same body) but huma documents only its
`DefaultStatus` (201), so ogen treated a 200 re-enroll as an unexpected status
and failed to decode it. `spec/normalize.go` (`addCreateCIWebhookReenrollStatus`)
rewrites that operation's success response to a `2XX` range, so ogen emits one
concrete `*CIWebhookViewStatusCode` — declaring 200 and 201 separately would
force a per-status sum type and break the `(*T, error)` ergonomics the rest of
the client relies on. The wrapper's `StatusCode` still distinguishes fresh from
re-enroll. Tracked as UPSTREAM.md item 3; the real fix is huma advertising the
200. The regenerated diff is confined to the enroll operation.

## What

## Summary

> **Status: Preview.** The integration ships with `IsPreview() == true` — users see a "(Preview)" label in the agent selector, `entire agent list`, and the hook-install message. Known limitations are listed below and in `docs/architecture/agent-guide.md` ("Antigravity status: Preview").

First-class support for **Antigravity CLI** (`agy`), Google's successor to Gemini CLI, as a new Entire agent — the complete integration: lifecycle hooks, transcript decoding, native token counts, review-skill discovery, resume tracking, docs, and E2E wiring. Consolidates the previously stacked PRs #1356 (tokens) and #1381 (transcript decode) plus the gap-fix and review-fix rounds into this single parent.

**Scope map** (~7.2k insertions; ~60% tests):

| Area | What |
|---|---|
| `cmd/entire/cli/agent/antigravity/` | agent package: 3 lifecycle hooks (`pre-tool-use`, `pre-invocation`, `stop`), transcript analyzers (prompts, positions, modified files), async-transcript handling, token tee (`statusline.go`/`title_install.go`), review-skill discovery |
| `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go`, `state.go`, `event.go` | conditional TurnStart (resume tracking), out-of-band token baseline/delta, committed-state filtering for mid-turn commits |
| `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/` | empty-transcript degrade (agy-scoped), late-flush prompt recovery, checkpoint-scoped token resolution, agy summary/count cases |
| `agent/skilldiscovery/` | shared SKILL.md scanner (claude-code rewired onto it) |
| e2e + CI | agy runner with three auth modes (ADC → `GEMINI_API_KEY` → OAuth), trusted-workspace seeding, fatal-vs-transient classification, agy-log + hook-probe artifact capture; **dispatch-only** in workflows (see limitations) |
| docs | CLAUDE/AGENTS, architecture guide quirks section, checklist, e2e README |

## Real-agy quirks (all hardened in code + tests)

- **`invocationNum` is 0-indexed**; PreInvocation fires per *model invocation*. `invocationNum > 0` emits a conditional TurnStart (`Event.SuppressIfSessionActive`) the dispatcher drops only when a turn is genuinely mid-flight — so resumes (`agy --conversation`) are tracked and follow-up invocations don't clobber the pre-prompt baseline.
- **agy writes its transcript AFTER `Stop`.** `PrepareTranscript` briefly waits then materializes a placeholder; condensation degrades to a files/prompt-only checkpoint (agy-scoped) and prompts are re-extracted late (`resolvePromptsFromLateFlushedTranscript`).
- **Tokens have exactly one surface** — the title/statusline JSON. The global `title` slot is claimed by `entire hooks antigravity title-tee` (wrap-preserving, doctor-checked); TurnStart snapshots a baseline, TurnEnd computes the delta (`OutOfBandTokenSource`).
- **Tool args are double-encoded**; `decodeAgyString`/`decodeAgyBool` tolerate both shapes. macOS `/tmp` symlinks resolved.
- **No SessionStart hook surface** → silent tracking (same as Cursor/OpenCode/Copilot/Pi). agy's PostToolUse/PostInvocation hooks are deliberately **not installed** — no lifecycle mapping, and they'd spawn a no-op subprocess per tool call.

## Review & verification

- Three-dimension agent review (correctness / over-engineering / hooks-and-docs-vs-agy-1.0.15) followed by a 28-agent adversarially-verified full-implementation review; **all 10 verified findings fixed** (token double-counting, tokens lost on fully-committed turns, deletion-filter regression, cross-worktree title-tee uninstall, e2e retry masking, degrade scoping, hook-prefix matching, + 3 cleanups).
- Hook contract verified byte-for-byte against agy's official docs (1.0.15 changed no hook behavior).
- Analyzer methods validated against **385 real captured agy transcripts: 0 errors, 0 offset mismatches**; full-pipeline replay of a real transcript reproduces prompts/files/checkpoint contents.
- Live smoke on this tip: `entire agent add antigravity` → real hook wiring → mid-turn commit with unwritten transcript → checkpoint + trailer + scoped tokens + `entire status` all correct. Real `agy` fired PreInvocation live (session state created); the model call itself is quota-gated (below).
- **2026-07-13 review round (3-reviewer pass + live testing on real agy)**: `TestSingleSessionManualCommit` passed live with real token counts; fresh-repo smoke verified install → live turn → commit → condensation → resume (`agy --conversation`) → token scoping across two commits. agy auto-updated 1.0.16→1.1.1 mid-session; hook wire contract re-verified unchanged, but agy 1.1 moved the skill-discovery directories — fixed, along with the ADC-mode quota-log peek, a doctor false-positive for non-agy teammates, an explicit Stop-hook timeout, and an `agent remove` warning about the global title-tee. Deferred minors are tracked as findings on trail 444.

> **Behavior note (all agents):** the ghost-session fix intentionally changes shadow-branch preservation — a read-only ACTIVE session (no tracked files) no longer keeps its shadow branch alive on commit (`phase_postcommit_test.go` updated accordingly). Both checkpoint writers skip zero-file writes, so nothing such a session wrote can be stranded.

## Known limitations (preview)

- **Live agy E2E runs in the default matrix in agy's Gemini API-key mode** (no account session; the shared `GEMINI_API_KEY` secret). agy ≤ 1.1.24 loaded `.agents/hooks.json` on that route but never executed the hooks (google-antigravity/antigravity-cli#893, still open upstream); bisecting the release binaries with a probe hook shows **agy ≥ 1.1.25 executes them**, and CI installs `releases/latest` (1.2.7 as of 2026-09-21). The optional `ANTIGRAVITY_GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS_JSON` secret still switches the leg to ADC; the `cloudcode-pa` backend remains entitlement-gated (subject 110002). Fail-fast classification covers quota/entitlement walls plus `GEMINI_API_KEY … not set` / `API_KEY_INVALID`. Details in `e2e/README.md`.
- **Transcript-derived file lists can be incomplete** when agy persists a step with `truncated_fields` and drops `TargetFile` (reported by @ecgang, ~0.8% of `replace_file_content` calls in their corpus). Now logged as a WARN per dropped call instead of a silent skip; live PreToolUse stdin is never truncated so only the late-flush / first-turn fallbacks are affected. Awaiting a real fixture.
- Mid-turn-commit checkpoints record zero tokens (the turn's delta lands on the next condensation — totals stay correct; documented at the fallback).
- No in-agy banner (no SessionStart hook surface) — tracking is silent inside the agy UI; `entire status` is the visibility surface.
- First-turn mid-turn commits can produce a files/prompt-only checkpoint (agy's transcript lands after Stop); prompts recover on the next condensation.
- Token capture depends on `entire hooks antigravity title-tee` owning/wrapping agy's global `title` slot (doctor-checked, setup-repaired).
- Wire format captured on agy 1.0.14/1.0.15, re-verified unchanged on agy 1.1.1 (2026-07-13) and 1.1.22 (2026-08-27: still exactly 5 hook types; statusline/title payload unchanged). agy is fast-moving — 1.1 moved the skill directories (handled), 1.1.10 fixed hook ordering so `Stop`/`PostInvocation` fire reliably, 1.1.12 answers `-p "/hooks"` locally (used by `entire doctor` to verify the workspace hooks actually load, zero quota).

## Test safety

- Every top-level test and subtest calls `t.Parallel()` unless it changes
  process-global state (`t.Chdir`, `t.Setenv`, or their `os` equivalents).
- Git tests use isolated temporary repositories, preferably
  `testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)` plus its file/add/commit helpers. Redirect CWD before
  calling CWD-based handlers. Never mutate the real checkout's git/session state.
- Tests must not access the developer's real config, cache, or keychain.
  In-process fallbacks are shared per process; use per-test overrides and
  `tokenstore.UseFileBackendForTesting` when isolation between tests is needed.
  Tests that can reach the OS keyring need `keyring.MockInit()` in `TestMain`.
- Spawned binaries do not inherit Go's test detection. Harnesses must isolate
  `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file`,
  `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH`, and `ENTIRE_TEST_AUTH_STORE_FILE`.
- Prefer `execx.NonInteractive` for real CLI/git test subprocesses so a developer's
  terminal cannot make them prompt or hang.
- Caller-resolution tests clear every variable from `agent.CallerSessionEnvVars()`;
  never hand-maintain a partial list or inherit the developer's agent identity.
- Source-scanning guards discover files through testutil's guard helpers
  (`GitGrepGuard`, `GuardGoFiles`), restrict pathspecs to Go files, and fail on
  zero matches. Do not weaken guard ledgers to silence failures.

## Filesystem and settings safety

**Use the existing anchor for each tree; never assemble a path and perform bare
I/O beneath it.** Read the filesystem reference before adding or changing I/O.

| Tree | Canonical owner |
| --- | --- |
| `.entire` | `entiredir` |
| Git common directory | `gitdir` |
| Working tree | `worktreedir` |
| Agent hook configuration | `agent.HookConfigFile` |
| Agent session store | `agent.SessionStore` |
| Active git hooks directory | `strategy.hooksRootForInstall` / `ForRemoval` |
| Per-user config/cache | `userdirs.ConfigRoot` / `CacheRoot` |
| Managed plugins | `pluginRoot` |

- Root bases come from trusted resolvers, **not `filepath.Dir(target)`**. Confining
  a file to its own derived parent proves nothing. Prefer an existing anchor.
- Roots share the `osroot.Shared` registry. Open child roots with
  `osroot.SharedChild` / `OpenChild`, not bare `parent.OpenRoot`.
- Use `osroot` operations and `jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn` / `CreateTempIn`.
  Directories use `MkdirAllNoSymlink`; rooted read-only operations must also
  enforce symlink policy. Atomic writes replace leaf links rather than follow them.
- `.entire` must be a real directory; validate through
  `paths.ValidateEntireDirAt` / `RequireEntireDir`. Do not treat an unresolved
  repository as absent. Settings reads must also refuse symlinks themselves.
- Do not broaden symlink exceptions. Developer-vouched agent config directories
  are scoped, locally trusted exceptions; `.entire` and git hooks are not vouchable.
- `entiredir.OpenForRead` must not create directories. Reset cached roots before
  deleting/recreating their directories. Use `entiredir.Name` / `MustName` to
  bridge repo-relative constants and root-relative I/O names.
- All settings access goes through `settings`; never read or parse settings JSON
  ad hoc. Per-user config/cache resolution belongs only to `userdirs`.
- Repository-controlled settings must not authorize executable discovery, custom
  executables, or instructions for permission-bypassed agents. Preserve the
  existing local-provenance gates and their rejection reporting.
- Existing exceptions (explicit user paths, global git config, transcript-read
  protocol gaps) are documented in the references; do not generalize them.

## Git and subprocess safety

- Open repositories only through `gitrepo.OpenCurrent(ctx)` or
  `gitrepo.OpenPath(root)`, never direct go-git opens. This preserves alternates
  and reftable support. Do not fall back to CWD after failed repo resolution.
- Use `gitrepo.Status`, never `worktree.Status()`. Agent-hook capture paths use
  `StatusWithBudget` and preserve degraded-capture reporting on budget exhaustion.
- Every `git status` subprocess passes **`--no-optional-locks`**. This does not
  protect worktree-comparing `git diff` from refreshing the index; use the
  hook-safe alternatives in the git reference.
- Use the git CLI, not go-git v5, for checkout and hard reset; go-git can delete
  ignored/untracked directories. This is an implementation rule, not permission
  to run destructive git commands.
- Git-relative paths resolve against `paths.WorktreeRoot`, never process CWD.
- A git subprocess targeting a repository independently of the current hook must
  use `gitrepo.EnvWithoutRepoOverrides()`; `Dir` or `-C` alone does not override
  inherited selectors. Queries inspecting the commit Git is preparing must retain
  the hook environment, including its temporary `GIT_INDEX_FILE`. Hook queries
  reading only the hook's own refs or reflog may strip selectors and resolve from
  `paths.WorktreeRoot`. User-invoked CWD commands also honor intentionally
  exported repo selectors.
- PATH scanners use `execx.PathScanDirs()`; external-agent execution requires
  absolute binary paths. User-directory overrides use the checked `userdirs`
  resolvers before any I/O.
- When Entire owns execution, pass arguments separately; never interpolate
  dynamic values into `cmd.exe`. Agent-owned shell execution uses the shared
  escaping helper. See the reference for the literal-only Unix updater exception.

## CLI behavior and output

- Load settings through the `settings` package, not new helpers in CLI consumers.
- Operational/debug messages use `logging.Debug/Info/Warn/Error`; user output uses
  `cmd.OutOrStdout()` / `cmd.ErrOrStderr()`. Never log prompts, file contents, or
  commit messages; log operational metadata only.
- Cobra suppresses errors globally; `main.go` prints returned errors. Return
  `NewSilentError(err)` only after printing a custom error yourself.
- Every read-only workflow must work without a TUI: provide complete text/JSON,
  stable IDs and detail commands, or direct selection flags. Test that path.
- Use `uiform.New` (or `NewAccessibleForm` in `cli`) for Huh forms; these wire
  accessibility and theming centrally. Do not hand-roll `WithAccessible`.
- Separately opened prompt terminals use `interactive.OpenPromptTTY()` and
  `PromptTTY.Close()`, not a bare file close (Windows pending reads can hang).
- Register experimental commands with `experimental.Register`. Classify new
  commands in `agentHelpClassification`; default to unlisted/user-owned and
  flag the product choice for review. Agent guidance belongs in `agentHelpGuidance`,
  not Cobra `Short`/`Long` or first-turn injection.

## Session, checkpoint, and API contracts

- `*strategy.ManualCommitStrategy` is the only strategy; there is no interface or
  worktree restore path. Turn ends write session state only; checkpoints are
  metadata refs written at commit, never working-branch commits. Log resume is distinct from restoring worktree files.
- Caller identity comes from `strategy.ResolveCallerSession`, not newest state.
  Preserve resolution provenance; do not narrate worktree fallback or ambiguous
  matches as identified callers. `IsCaller()` excludes those guesses; consult
  the caller-resolution reference for current enforcement gaps.
- Preserve sanitize → image drop or externalization → redact ordering where all apply,
  fail-closed scanner behavior, and checkpoint-scoped token accounting. Read the
  implementation contracts before modifying any transcript/storage pipeline.
- Control-plane precedence belongs to `coreapi`; display `client.CoreOrigin()`
  rather than independently resolving a possibly different target.
- Repo-scoped data-plane requests resolve the repo's cell and fail on resolution
  failure. `/me` uses the home cell; repo-set queries use shared fanout helpers.
  Multi-cell operations share one `auth.CellClientFactory` per operation.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#MISE description="Fail on functions this branch made new or worse than the base (cognitive complexity > 30)"
set -euo pipefail

# The blocking half of the complexity gate, run identically here and in CI
# (.github/workflows/ci.yml calls this task). It compares the working tree
# against the merge base with BASE_REF and fails on functions that are both
# over the threshold and new or worsened; the repo's long tail of pre-existing
# violations is deliberately exempt. See tools/complexity/README.md.
#
# BASE_REF     ref to take the merge base with (default origin/main; CI passes
#              the pull request's base SHA)
# COGNIT_WARN  the threshold (default 30)

BASE_REF="${BASE_REF:-origin/main}"
COGNIT_WARN="${COGNIT_WARN:-30}"

repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$repo_root"

if ! base_sha="$(git merge-base "$BASE_REF" HEAD)"; then
  echo "error: no merge base between $BASE_REF and HEAD (fetch it first: git fetch origin main)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
# --no-optional-locks per the repo rule: `git status` otherwise rewrites the
# index, and this can run while an agent's hooks are touching the same repo.
# Untracked files count as a change, because a new .go file is exactly what
# this gate exists to look at and `git diff` would not see it.
if [ "$base_sha" = "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ] && [ -z "$(git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain)" ]; then
  echo "complexity gate: working tree is the merge base with $BASE_REF — nothing to compare"
  exit 0
fi

tmpdir="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT

# `git archive` rather than `git worktree add`: this task is meant to be run
# from a dirty working tree, and an export leaves no entry in the repo's
# worktree list to clean up if it is interrupted. The repo has no
# .gitattributes, so the export is a faithful copy of the tree.
mkdir -p "$tmpdir/basetree"
git archive "$base_sha" | tar -x -C "$tmpdir/basetree"

# Both runs use the HEAD version of the tool and of the feature mapping, so
# cxtool can evolve without a change to it looking like a complexity change.
cd tools/complexity
go build -o "$tmpdir/cxtool" .
go build -o "$tmpdir/gate" ./gate

# No -cover: the diff reads only per-function complexity, and skipping the
# coverage profiles (and churn, which needs a git dir the export does not
# have) keeps each run to about a second. cxtool's stderr is left alone — it
# lists unmapped files there, and swallowing it would swallow its errors too.
"$tmpdir/cxtool" -root "$tmpdir/basetree" -churn-days '' -out "$tmpdir/base"
"$tmpdir/cxtool" -root "$repo_root" -churn-days '' -out "$tmpdir/head"

echo "complexity gate: HEAD vs $(git -C "$repo_root" rev-parse --short "$base_sha") (merge base with $BASE_REF)"
"$tmpdir/gate" -base "$tmpdir/base" -head "$tmpdir/head" -cognit-warn "$COGNIT_WARN"

An idle `entire mcp` process answers ping but survives the first SIGTERM while its host keeps stdin open. The root context is cancelled, but the scanner remains blocked in its input read. This interrupts that read and lets the existing signal handler finish shutdown.

## Reproduction

The issue includes a standalone Python supervisor that waits for a ping reply, keeps stdin open and sends SIGTERM. No agent or credentials are needed.

| | First SIGTERM | Second SIGTERM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upstream `e362dd9f9` | Still alive | Exits with signal 15 |
| This change | Exits with signal 15 | Unnecessary |

A host that closes stdin already avoids this particular hang. Blocked output writes are outside this fix's scope.

## Change

- Give the server ownership of a closeable input and close it once on return.
- Reuse the existing `cancelreader` dependency on Unix to interrupt inherited blocking stdin. Regular files and non-terminal character devices retain direct reads to avoid kqueue EOF waits.
- On Windows, use Go's pipe-close cancellation; `cancelreader` would open console input instead of preserving redirected stdin.
- Keep scanning on the serving goroutine and wait for any running cancellation callback before releasing polling resources. Return the context error so existing signal exit behavior is preserved.

The commits separate the four-file fix/unit tests from the one-file inherited-stdin process regression. The process regression reuses the existing main() subprocess harness, isolates configuration, waits for ping and checks actual first-SIGTERM termination for idle and incomplete-message input. #MISE description="Lint for secret-shaped literals that remote push protection rejects"

# Some credential shapes are rejected by the forge on push, not merely flagged.
# GitHub push protection refuses an AWS Access Key ID outright, and because this
# repo stores its own agent transcripts as checkpoints and pushes them, one such
# literal in a test fixture reaches a transcript whenever someone edits redaction

# was just written and not yet staged, which a plain git grep never sees. Exit 1
# from git grep means no matches; anything above 1 is git itself failing, and
# a guard that passes because git failed is worse than no guard.
hits="$(git grep --untracked -InE 'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}' -- .)"
status=$?
if [ "$status" -gt 1 ]; then
  echo "git grep failed (exit $status)" >&2
  exit "$status"
fi

if [ -n "$hits" ]; then
  echo "Secret-shaped literals found that push protection will reject:"
  echo ""
  echo "$hits"
  echo ""
  echo "Assemble the value at runtime instead of inlining it."
  echo "See redact.awsKeyFixture in redact/redact_test.go."
  exit 1
fi
